---
title: "Inspect build history"
---

This command is in development source, after installed preview.3.

~~~bash
proj history
proj history --limit 10
proj history --attempt attempt-0123456789abcdefghijklmn
proj --machine history
~~~

The summary shows the newest recorded attempts first, ordered by start
time with an ID tie-breaker. --attempt lists final observed file names,
logical labels and existing MD5 byte hashes, including empty-directory markers.
It works without Git or active configuration. It reads evidence without acquiring
a build lock, changing versions, rerunning analysis or contacting a remote.

Each new final observation retains `.proj/log/ATTEMPT_ID.final.csv` in the existing
label,fn,version,hash format. Its JSON record or Git outcome receipt binds its
exact bytes and canonical inventory fingerprint. End hooks may change files:
these final rows describe the observation after finalization was attempted,
separately from the release inventory. They do not prove that files still exist,
authenticate another person's record, or verify remote availability.

With optional Git, the final CSV and outcome receipt join the **next normal
commit**. The pre-Git record remains unchanged; no recursive bookkeeping commit
is created. Only an intact, locally witnessed receipt/CSV bundle qualifies for
the narrow pending-evidence exception. Missing or altered companions fail closed.

For earlier records containing only inventory fingerprints, detailed rows are
available from project manifest.csv only when the release, labels, counts and
canonical fingerprint match exactly. Otherwise they are unavailable. A pending
pre-Git snapshot without a terminal receipt remains unresolved.

Human output is Markdown on stdout, safely quoting file names. Redirect it to a
file if useful; proj does not rewrite BUILDLOG.md or the curated changelog.
The machine envelope contains result.history.entries; details add
final_files.source and final_files.rows. Summary queries omit detailed rows.

Queries allow 1–100 summaries (default 20), scan at most 10,000 log directory
entries and accept at most 64 MiB total JSON, 1 MiB per JSON file and 16 MiB/
100,000 rows per selected CSV. New final CSV retention uses the same CSV limits.
Malformed records, linked paths, mismatched receipts and corrupted selected CSVs
are errors. Disabled/failed observations are not empty inventories.

Previews and pre-distribution failures retain their existing behavior. No
failure-retention, pruning, registry or remote policy is chosen here.
